grid_rules: [Alberta's Data Centre Strategy](https://www.alberta.ca/artificial-intelligence-data-centres-strategy) (December 2024) highlights the plan to position the province as an attractive location to build data centers. This includes three pillars, power capacity, sustainable cooling, and economic growth. [The Alberta Electric System Operator](https://www.aeso.ca/grid/connecting-to-the-grid/large-load-projects) capped new large power users at 1,200 MW for now (Phase 1). Alberta's [Utilities Statutes Amendment Act](https://www.alberta.ca/powering-new-pathways-for-data-centres) (Royal Assent Dec 11, 2025) will also encourage data centers to bring their own power.
check_status: Checked: AESO page lists 2 projects (970 + 230 MW); Bill 8 date + BYOP priority confirmed (Bennett Jones)

grid_rules: Ontario's [Data Centre Playbook](https://news.ontario.ca/assets/files/20260813/652439f5209093b5a8a7f0f12c795c1e.pdf) (Aug 2026) has a framework for the province to attract data center assessments. The playbook has three principles. Data centers must invest in communities, pay full electricity costs, and the province will only offer non-financial support to data centers. Ontario's [Bill 40](https://ero.ontario.ca/notice/025-1001) (Royal Assent Dec 11, 2025) amended the Electricity Act, which allowed the province to prioritize and approve data center requests that serve the province's best interests.
check_status: Checked: Royal Assent Dec 11, 2025; no thresholds set yet (Torys)

grid_rules: Saskatchewan's Data Centre Framework (Aug 27, 2026) specifies that new data centers need to supply their own power. The framework also includes six principles including Canadian ownership, Canadian data and AI sovereignty, jobs and partnerships, industry experience, power generation, and a centralized intake process.
check_status: Grid rules checked against Government of Saskatchewan news release, Nov 13, 2026. Other fields from York Table 2.

grid_rules: [PacifiCan's Strategic Plan](https://www.canada.ca/en/pacific-economic-development/corporate/transparency/departmental-reports-other/strategic-plans/strategic-plan-2026-2028.html) lists AI as a key opportunity for British Columbia. In 2025, British Columbia passed the Energy Statutes Amendment Act (Bill 31), which allowed the province to create a new [Electricity Allocation Framework](https://www2.gov.bc.ca/gov/content/industry/electricity-alternative-energy/electricity/industrial-electricity-allocation-framework) to prioritize electricity for projects that provide the most benefits to the province.

grid_rules: In November 2026, the province issued a new [Data Centre Policy](https://www.gnb.ca/en/news/n-b.2026.11.government-adopts-stringent-approval-process-for-proposed-data-centres.html) which set priorities and criteria for new data center projects. These priorities include meaningful engagement with First Nations and communities, data centers must minimize impact on the environment and communities, and must bring economic value to the province.

grid_rules: No data center strategy. Yukon's electricity grid is not connected to the North American grid in British Columbia. Most of its power comes from hydro, with some fossil fuels and biomass ([Canada Energy Regulator](https://www.cer-rec.gc.ca/en/data-analysis/energy-markets/provincial-territorial-energy-profiles/provincial-territorial-energy-profiles-yukon.html)). A data center there would likely have to generate its own power.

grid_rules: No data center strategy. The Northwest Territories does not have one electricity grid for the whole territory. It has two regional grids that do not connect to each other, and 25 smaller local systems ([Canada Energy Regulator](https://www.cer-rec.gc.ca/en/data-analysis/energy-markets/provincial-territorial-energy-profiles/provincial-territorial-energy-profiles-northwest-territories.html)). A data center there would likely have to generate its own power.
